faqs.question: What is the Zeiss Axioscan 7 used for?
faqs.answer: It's an automated digital slide scanner, used across life science research, pharma and biotech spatial biology, clinical diagnostics, and geology, digitizing microscope slides at high throughput.

faqs.question: How many slides can it scan in one run?
faqs.answer: Up to 100, depending on the configuration, with reliable 24/7 unattended operation.

faqs.question: What configurations are available?
faqs.answer: Four: Standard (Life Science Research), Spatial Biology (Pharma & Biotech), Clinical, and Geology and Materials, each with different slide formats, contrast techniques, and software integration.

faqs.question: Is Axioscan 7 certified for clinical diagnostic use?
faqs.answer: Only the Clinical configuration carries IVDR certification. The Standard, Spatial Biology, and Geology configurations are not certified for diagnostic use.

faqs.question: What contrast techniques are supported?
faqs.answer: Up to five, depending on configuration: brightfield, fluorescence, circular polarization, crossed linear polarization, and TIE (transport of intensity equation).

faqs.question: How many objectives are available?
faqs.answer: Up to 14 on Standard and Geology configurations, 3 on Spatial Biology, and 2 base objectives with 4 additional options on Clinical.

faqs.question: What software does it use?
faqs.answer: ZEN, or third-party solutions, on Standard and Geology. Spatial Biology adds SlideStream software and Mindpeak AI-based image analysis. Clinical integrates into IMS/PACS systems via ZEISS Solutions Lab and a Dicom converter.

faqs.question: Can it handle multiple staining rounds on the same tissue?
faqs.answer: Yes, on the Spatial Biology configuration, which supports coregistration of multiple staining rounds alongside Mindpeak AI-based analysis.

faqs.question: What slide formats are supported?
faqs.answer: 1x3", 2x3", and 4x3" on Standard and Geology (Geology adds GEO format specifically), 1x3" only on Spatial Biology and Clinical.

faqs.question: Is this suitable for geological or petrographic work?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Geology configuration supports GEO-format slides and pairs with the Petrography Analysis Toolbox (PetPAT) for quantitative analytics.

faqs.question: How does the Clinical configuration connect to hospital systems?
faqs.answer: Via ZEISS Solutions Lab and a Dicom converter, integrating into existing IMS and PACS infrastructure. Zeiss notes this integration path itself is not an in vitro diagnostic device.

faqs.question: Where can I find detailed technical specifications?
faqs.answer: Full technical specifications, including dimensions, weight and objective and camera part numbers, are available from Inkarp on request.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Axioscan 7 in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the configuration, objectives, and software selected.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the Axioscan 7 in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Zeiss Axioscan 7 in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

sections.title: Four Configurations, One Platform
sections.tabSummary: Choosing between Standard, Spatial Biology, Clinical, and Geology
body: Choosing between Standard, Spatial Biology, Clinical, and Geology.

Buying an automated slide scanner sized for a general lab, then trying to run clinical diagnostic samples or multi-round spatial biology staining through it, means fighting the hardware and software the whole way. Axioscan 7 avoids that by not being one general-purpose system, Zeiss builds four distinct configurations, each with its own slide format range, contrast technique set, objective count, and software layer.

Standard covers the broadest general research use, up to 14 objectives and the full contrast range including crossed linear polarization. Spatial Biology trades objective breadth (down to 3) for SlideStream software and Mindpeak AI, purpose-built for coregistering multiple staining rounds and running AI-based analysis at scale. Clinical narrows the slide format to 1x3" only and adds direct IMS/PACS integration, with the IVDR certification that makes diagnostic use possible. Geology keeps Standard's broad objective and contrast range but adds GEO format slide support for petrographic work.

paragraphs: A slide scanner used for research doesn't need regulatory certification to produce useful images. A slide scanner used to inform an actual clinical diagnosis does, and that's a genuinely different bar to clear, one the Standard, Spatial Biology, and Geology configurations explicitly don't claim to meet.

Axioscan 7 Clinical carries IVDR certification, In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation, the EU framework governing diagnostic devices. It integrates directly into hospital IMS and PACS systems through ZEISS Solutions Lab and a Dicom converter, so scanned slides enter the same digital pathology workflow radiology and lab systems already use. Zeiss is explicit that this integration path itself is not an in vitro diagnostic device on its own, the certification sits specifically with the Clinical configuration.

faqs.question: What is the Zeiss Celldiscoverer 7 used for?
faqs.answer: It's an automated live-cell imaging platform, used for explorative high-content research, including cell biology, organoid research, developmental biology, and high-content screening.

faqs.question: Do I need to be a microscopy expert to use it?
faqs.answer: No. Insert the sample carrier and the system makes all necessary settings automatically, including calibration, focus, and aberration correction.

faqs.question: How much faster is the latest generation?
faqs.answer: Up to 9x faster widefield acquisition and up to 1.8x faster confocal acquisition, compared to the previous generation.

faqs.question: What is Autoimmersion?
faqs.answer: Fully automated water immersion supply and removal through a 50x objective, sealed with an elastic silicon membrane, supporting live-cell imaging at 37°C over several days.

faqs.question: What is Autocorr?
faqs.answer: Automatic correction ring adjustment on the objective, compensating for spherical aberration caused by different vessel bottom thickness or material.

faqs.question: Can it handle different sample carrier types?
faqs.answer: Yes, automatic sample recognition detects relevant vessel features on loading, supporting Petri dishes, chamber slides, multi-well plates, plastic or glass, thin or thick bottoms, and low- or high-skirt plates.

faqs.question: How does focus work for long time-lapse experiments?
faqs.answer: Find Focus locates the region of interest with one click; Definite Focus holds that position throughout the experiment, whether it runs seconds or several days, and automatic focus maps support multiple positions simultaneously.

faqs.question: Can it do confocal imaging?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the optional LSM 910 and Airyscan 2 upgrade, delivering up to 1.9x resolution improvement, spectral imaging, and photomanipulation techniques like FRAP and FRET.

faqs.question: Is there protection against objective damage?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Adaptive Lens Guard prevents collisions with the sample vessel or hardware while automatically maximizing the available scanning area.

faqs.question: Can throughput be increased with automation?
faqs.answer: Yes, an optional robotic sample loader from Peak Analysis & Automation (PAA) handles all SBS multi-well plate formats for high-volume, unattended processing.

faqs.question: What software analyzes the imaging data?
faqs.answer: arivis Pro, for 2D through complex 3D and 4D dataset analysis, with arivis Cloud for neural network training and arivis Hub for parallel cloud-based processing across multiple datasets.

faqs.question: Is it reliable in a shared, multi-user lab?
faqs.answer: Yes, workflows execute reproducibly without manual recalibration between users, and predictive service analytics schedule maintenance based on actual component wear.

faqs.question: How is Celldiscoverer 7 different from Axioscan 7?
faqs.answer: Celldiscoverer 7 automates live-cell and high-content imaging, with immersion, incubation, and focus systems built for living, dynamic samples. Axioscan 7 automates digitization of fixed, prepared slides at high volume, with no equivalent need for immersion or incubation.

faqs.question: Where can I find detailed technical specifications?
faqs.answer: Full technical specifications, including the full objective range and physical dimensions, are available from Inkarp on request.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Celldiscoverer 7 in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote based on the platform tier, confocal upgrade, and automation options selected.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the Celldiscoverer 7 in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Zeiss Celldiscoverer 7 in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

sections.tabSummary: What Autocorr and automatic sample recognition actually solve
body: What Autocorr and automatic sample recognition actually solve.

High-numerical-aperture objectives, the kind live-cell imaging genuinely needs, only deliver their promised contrast and sensitivity when their optics correctly compensate for the specific vessel they're looking through. Bottom thickness varies. Material varies, plastic versus glass. Skirt height varies between plate designs. Every one of those variations introduces spherical aberration if left uncorrected, and manually adjusting a correction ring for each new vessel type is exactly the kind of expertise-gated step that slows a lab down.

Celldiscoverer 7 removes it. Automatic sample recognition detects the relevant vessel features the moment a sample loads, and Autocorr adjusts the objective's correction ring to compensate, without anyone touching a dial. The freedom that unlocks is real: Petri dishes, chamber slides, multi-well plates, plastic or glass, thin or thick vessel bottoms, low-skirt or high-skirt plates, all usable interchangeably, at full optical quality, on the same system.

sections.title: Autoimmersion and Long-Term Live Imaging
sections.description: What multi-day, water-immersed experiments actually require.

cards.title: Immersion optics matched to aqueous samples
A sealed chamber protecting both sample and system
Stable temperature across days of imaging

paragraphs: Cell biology samples are mostly water, or mounted in aqueous solution, and high-resolution imaging of them needs immersion optics to match. Manual water immersion is tedious at best, and at worst it introduces exactly the kind of inconsistency that undermines a multi-day time-lapse.

Celldiscoverer 7 pairs an outstanding 50x water immersion objective with rapid automated immersion supply and removal, so that step disappears from the workflow entirely. An elastic silicon membrane seals the sample chamber during imaging, cutting unnecessary airflow while protecting the system from liquid spillage. Combined with sustained 37°C incubation, the result is genuinely unbiased live-cell experiments running over several days, or extensive automated scanning across entire multi-well plates, without a human needing to intervene partway through.
